description: v1 captures the envelope wrapper plus SeriesEvaluation, the payload emitted by check commit, check range, check merge, and check patch. Series-wide verdicts, per-pin verdict rows, diagnostics, and patch_facts are all in scope.

command.description: Verb identifier in kebab-case, e.g. "check merge".

oneOf.description: Variable identifier (starts with `_` or capital letter).
Atom literal: `foo`, `'quoted atom'`.
Integer literal.
Float literal.
Binary literal: `<<...>>`.
List literal: `[...]`.
Tuple literal: `{...}` (size is the number of elements).
Record reference: `#name{...}`.
String literal: `"..."`.
Anonymous fun: `fun ... end` or `fun mod:f/A`.
Anything the extractor cannot classify. Always matches.
`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`, or `||||||| ` marker present in a touched file. The cherry-pick driver left a conflict unresolved.
`-export([f/N])` line without a matching clause defining `f/N`. Compiles, then crashes at runtime on the first call.
`<<<<<<<` line: start of the local side.
`=======` line: divider between sides.
`>>>>>>>` line: end of the incoming side.
`||||||| ` line: base ancestor marker from a 3-way diff.

Diagnostics.description: Series-wide diagnostic envelope. Strictly separate from `Verdict` so untracked-call signals never leak into machine-readable verdicts.

suggested_suites.description: SUITE names worth running for the patch, derived from touched paths. Populated even when the verdict promotes to `Inapplicable` so that schema-only and config-only diffs still surface relevant suites.

oneOf.description: Every changed `.erl` hunk is a Variant A unwrap: dropping `-ifdef(TEST).` or `-endif.` around an `-export(...)` directive, or rewriting `-compile(export_all).` to an explicit `-export([...])`. No call sites, no specs, no bodies touched — only test-visibility metadata.

The patch touches Erlang surface but every referenced symbol resolves to the self-pin or to a local definition: every tracked-dep pin sees zero in-scope references. Without this reason the operator would see a wall of vacuous `Compatible` rows for a patch that backhopper genuinely has no signal on.

Every touched path lives in a sibling project's scope, not this pin's. The pin has nothing to say about the patch. `project` names the first sibling project (alphabetical) that owns the out-of-scope paths.
Every touched path is unclaimed by any configured project's scan_paths or app_roots. Vendored files, docs, build scripts.
`--target-repo-dir-path` was supplied and every touched path is missing from the target tree, with no configured translation mapping any of them. The patch as written does not apply to the target.

PatchFacts.description: Source classifiers on the patch. Strictly separate from `Verdict` reasons.

oneOf.description: The contiguous preimage block (Context and Removed lines from the hunk) was found verbatim at a different starting line. Cherry-pick adapters handle this with the `-x` trailer; the operator just needs the delta to confirm the patch's intent still applies.

The preimage block does not appear anywhere in the file. The patch was authored against a tree where the lines existed; on this pin they don't. Structurally inapplicable: the operator needs an excerpt to reason about why.

Call-site argument shapes don't satisfy any clause head at the pin. Emitted when both the call and the pin's clause patterns are concrete enough to compare; `Unknown` on either side is the escape hatch that suppresses the reason.
Patch references an MFA owned by the self-project but absent from the resolved self-snapshot. `suggested_source_for_prereq` is filled only with `--suggest-prereqs`.
Pre-flight syntactic damage in a touched file: an unresolved merge-conflict marker, an exported function with no definition, etc.
Patch changes a `-callback` signature; an implementer still has the old one.
Patch removes a required callback; implementer still exports it.
Patch adds a required callback; implementer is missing the export.
Patch touches a path absent on pin, but a module of the same basename exists elsewhere.
Wire-bearing macro value differs between source and pin.
`version/0` advanced without the matching historical-implementation module.
Function bodies drifted at the same advertised `version/0`. Mixed-version cluster risk.
`version/0` decreased pin → patch.
Spec return shape differs between source and pin for a referenced MFA.

A type-reference inside a `-spec`, `-callback`, `-type`, or `-opaque` attribute resolves to a name and arity that the pin does not expose via `-export_type`. Non-blocking: a missing type alias is a dialyzer-level concern, not a load-time crash.

A touched path is absent from the target tree, but a configured `[[path_translation]]` rewrites it to a path that does exist on the target. Non-blocking: the operator (or the cherry-pick driver) rewrites the path before applying.

TouchedKinds.description: Per-pin tally of file kinds the patch touched. Lets `promote_inapplicable` tell a real green check from a diff with nothing analyzable to check.

only_self_surface.description: The patch touches Erlang surface but references no tracked-dep API (every non-self pin sees zero in-scope references). The CLI sets this after `evaluate_series` when a self-pin is present and every non-self pin's `tracked_refs` is empty; see `InapplicableReason::OnlySelfSurfaceTouched`.

only_test_visibility.description: Every changed `.erl` hunk is a Variant A unwrap of test-only `-ifdef(TEST)` machinery around an `-export` directive (see `InapplicableReason::OnlyTestVisibilityChanged`). When true, the patch touches Erlang surface but adds no semantic content, so an empty reason set should promote to `Inapplicable` instead of `Compatible`.

Unanalyzed.description: Counts of call sites the analyzer could not resolve: `apply/3`-style BIFs, and dispatch through a variable module or function. Informational only.

data.description: The output of `Patch::evaluate_series`: verdicts plus diagnostics plus `PatchFacts` (source classifiers that drive downstream policy without being verdict reasons).
data.title: SeriesEvaluation

exit_code.description: Process exit code carried inside the envelope; matches the process status.

schema_version.description: Wire-format schema version. Bumps when envelope shape changes.

warnings.description: Free-form CLI warnings attached to the envelope.
